CVE-2026-105481.description:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP Agent connection reuse can cause a client to accept as valid a response that was sent before the client has sent the request. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48931.

The guard that destroys idle keep-alive sockets when unexpected data arrives only runs when the event loop polls for I/O. If an unsolicited response has already reached the socket but has not been read yet when the socket is handed to a new request, for example because the event loop was busy with synchronous work, the guard is removed without seeing it and the data is parsed as the response to the new request.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Fix the bypass dispatch claim for schedulers bypassed by an ancestor

scx_bypass() claims bypass dispatch when the scheduler's depth goes from
zero to one and releases it when the depth returns to zero, but propagates
only the depth to the descendants, not the claim. A descendant that starts

starts under a PM suspend has no claim, so once the resume lifts the root's

CVE-2026-99445.title: power: supply: pf1550: drain IRQ work before unregistering supplies
CVE-2026-99445.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: supply: pf1550: drain IRQ work before unregistering supplies

The VBUS work calls power_supply_changed(), but its managed
cancellation is registered before the supplies. Cleanup can therefore
unregister a supply while IRQ-triggered work is still pending.

Commit 838767f50747 ("power: supply: pf1550: Fix use-after-free in
power_supply_changed()") moved IRQ requests after supply registration,
but left work cancellation before the supplies. That change protects
the direct IRQ callbacks, while this fix drains the work they queue.

Register the three work items after both supplies and before the IRQs.
Cleanup then frees the IRQ producers, drains the work, and unregisters
the supplies.

The teardown ordering issue was found by static analysis.

CVE-2026-99768.title: wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()
CVE-2026-99768.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()

The commit 592234e941f1 ("wifi: mac80211: Fix iTXQ AMPDU fragmentation
handling") changed the way handling of the IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag
is done in mac80211, so the only place it is set is in
ieee80211_tx_dequeue().

This means that any frames that are sent to the driver via drv_tx() will
no longer have the flag set. In particular, this affects packets going
through ieee80211_tx_pending(). Evan reported that this can result in
the ath9k driver failing to account such packets in its block ack
window, eventually overrunning the window and stalling TX.

Fix this by reinstating the flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg() when inside
a valid block ack window. This should be harmless for the TXQ path, and
will reinstate the previous behaviour for drivers that use the flag as a
signal to track the packet in the window.
